headline: Microsoft surges 5.7% last night on cloud optimism while the ASX had a solid session up 0.68% — but GOOG dipped 2.2% ahead of Monday earnings.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft jumped 5.7% last night — a big single-session move. The market is pricing in strong expectations ahead of its July earnings date, particularly around cloud (Azure) growth. Investors are increasingly backing Microsoft's AI integration story, and with earnings coming up, momentum traders are piling in. Still sitting 15.8% below your average buy-in price, but this session cut a meaningful chunk off that gap.

movers.name: Alphabet (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped 2.2% last night. With earnings on the calendar for Monday US time, some investors are trimming positions ahead of the result — a common 'sell the news' setup. Microsoft's strong run may also be pulling AI sentiment away from Alphabet right now. You're still up ~8.9% overall on this position.

movers.name: Vanguard Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE had a solid day today, gaining 1.5%. Emerging markets got a boost from a steady AUD/USD and positive sentiment across Asian markets. You're essentially break-even on this holding overall.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market ETF
movers.note: VTS gained about 1% today, riding on last night's broadly positive US market tone. This ETF tracks the entire US share market, so Microsoft's big night helped lift it. Up 2.5% on your total investment.

movers.name: Global X AI ETF
movers.note: GXAI nudged up 0.9% today. AI-focused stocks continue to find buyers, though the ETF is still down about 6.3% from your purchase price. Microsoft's AI momentum is a positive signal for this holding.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: PLS edged up 0.8% today. Kalkine Media noted PLS is being watched as a bellwether for the broader ASX lithium revival — the sector has been bouncing after a brutal selloff. That said, you're still down 24.6% on this position, so it's a long road back.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG gained 0.7% today — a steady, unexciting move in the right direction. As a diversified fund spread across global shares, it benefits from broad market tailwinds. Up 2.3% on your total investment.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy ETF
movers.note: FUEL dipped 0.7% today despite oil prices actually rising about 1% overnight. The slight lag is likely timing — the ASX session didn't fully capture last night's oil bounce. Crude oil is sitting at US$69.93/barrel.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO was essentially flat last night, barely moving. The GTA 6 hype is keeping a floor under the stock — pre-order momentum is building — but there was news that disc editions of GTA 6 may not be happening, which could have taken a little wind out of the sails of physical retail excitement.

watch_today.title: GOOG earnings on Monday US time — decision point
watch_today.detail: Alphabet reports earnings on Monday night US time (Tuesday AEST). The stock has already dipped 2.2% last night, possibly as traders take profits ahead of the result. If Google's cloud and AI revenue growth disappoints, there could be further downside. If it beats — especially on AI products — expect a sharp bounce. Worth watching closely if you're thinking about adding or trimming.

watch_today.title: MSFT — big move last night, earnings coming in July
watch_today.detail: Microsoft jumped 5.7% last night — its best session in a while. The market is getting excited about the July earnings update, especially for Azure cloud and AI products (like Copilot). You're still down 15.8% overall but this is a meaningful recovery move. Hold and watch; the July earnings print will be the real test.

watch_today.title: RBA holds rates — good news for Australian stocks
watch_today.detail: The Reserve Bank of Australia left interest rates on hold today. This is a relief for mortgage holders and generally positive for the share market — lower rates (or no new hikes) tend to make shares more attractive. The AFR is even reporting that near-zero rates could be closer than most expect. Good backdrop for your ASX holdings like VDHG, VGE, and VTS.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium bounce, but still deep in the red
watch_today.detail: Pilbara Minerals is up 0.8% today and is being talked up as a leader in the ASX lithium sector recovery. But you're still down 24.6% on your investment. The sector revival narrative is real but fragile — lithium prices need to stabilise for this to stick. Hold for now and watch for any update on lithium spot prices out of China.

watch_today.title: TTWO — GTA 6 release approaching, but no disc edition
watch_today.detail: Take-Two is almost flat but there's a news item circulating that GTA 6 physical disc editions won't be happening, per a Rockstar source. That's a modest negative for retail sales optics, but digital pre-orders are reportedly building momentum. The real share price catalyst will be the actual game launch. Hold and watch.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX — oil bounced overnight, ETF lagged
watch_today.detail: Crude oil (WTI) rose 1% overnight to US$69.93/barrel, but your FUEL energy ETF actually fell 0.7% today — the ASX session didn't fully reflect the oil move. If oil holds its gains, FUEL could play catch-up in tomorrow's session. Keep an eye on it.

markets.summary: The ASX 200 had a good day today, closing up 0.68% at 8,823 — helped by the RBA holding interest rates steady, which gave investors confidence. Last night on Wall Street, the S&P 500 was nearly flat (down just 0.05%) and the NASDAQ slipped 0.24%, but the action was really in individual stocks — Microsoft's 5.7% surge dominated headlines. Oil ticked up 1% to nearly US$70 a barrel. Gold eased slightly. The Aussie dollar is holding steady around US$0.69.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed up today — RBA holding rates steady gave investors a confidence boost.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Essentially flat last night — the broad US market trod water.

indicators.name: NASDAQ
indicators.note: Slight dip last night despite Microsoft surging — drag from Google and other tech names.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil bounced about 1% last night — positive for energy stocks.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold eased slightly — investors in a mild risk-on mood.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: Virtually unchanged — the Aussie dollar is steady around 69 US cents.

politics.summary: The RBA dominated Australian news today, holding interest rates steady and signalling it's better prepared for future crises. The Albanese Government also made a big move on teen social media, doubling penalties for platforms that allow under-16s to sign up.

stories.title: RBA holds interest rates steady — and near-zero rates may be closer than you think
stories.why_it_matters: The Reserve Bank left the cash rate on hold at its meeting today — relief for mortgage holders who were watching nervously. More importantly, the AFR is reporting that internal RBA briefings suggest near-zero interest rates could be on the horizon sooner than markets expected. That's a big deal: cheaper borrowing costs tend to lift share prices and property values, and reduce the pressure on household budgets.

stories.title: RBA prepares 'fire drills' for the next COVID-like economic crisis
stories.why_it_matters: RBA Assistant Governor Chris Kent said today that the central bank is running 'fire drills' — practice scenarios — to make sure it can respond faster if another pandemic-style economic shock hits. The RBA's COVID response was criticised for being slow and then overcorrecting with rate hikes that hammered borrowers. The bank wants to show it's learned from that experience.

stories.title: Albanese Government doubles penalty to $99m for tech giants over under-16 social media rules
stories.why_it_matters: The Albanese Government has doubled the maximum fine for tech platforms that allow users under 16 to sign up to social media — now up to $99 million per breach. This ramps up the pressure on platforms like Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat to actually enforce age verification. For investors holding tech/social media stocks, this signals Australia is getting serious about digital regulation, and global platforms are watching.

ai.summary: AI regulation dominated the global AI conversation today, with polls showing bipartisan public support for tighter rules. The debate is shifting from 'should we regulate AI?' to 'how do we regulate it without killing innovation?'

stories.title: Voters of both US parties want tighter AI regulation, new poll finds
stories.why_it_matters: A new NBC News poll found that Americans across the political spectrum — both Republican and Democrat voters — want stronger guardrails on AI. This is notable because AI regulation has become one of the rare bipartisan issues in the US. For investors in AI-exposed stocks like GOOG, MSFT, and GXAI.AX, this signals that some form of US federal AI regulation is increasingly likely, which could add compliance costs but also legitimise the industry.

stories.title: Guardrails, not a 'Licence Raj': The debate over how to regulate AI without strangling it
stories.why_it_matters: Policy commentators are warning that heavy-handed AI regulation could create a 'Licence Raj' — a reference to India's old over-regulated bureaucratic system that stifled business. The argument is that governments should set guardrails (safety rules, transparency requirements) without requiring companies to get government sign-off before deploying new AI tools. This debate will shape how quickly AI products reach consumers and businesses.

stories.title: Lifetime access to ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and more for under $60 — deal doing the rounds
stories.why_it_matters: A deal doing the rounds offers lifetime access to multiple AI tools — ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, Anthropic's Claude and others — for a one-off payment of under US$60. It's a sign of how commoditised AI assistant access is becoming. For everyday users, this means all-you-can-eat AI is now cheaper than a monthly Netflix sub. For the big AI companies, the race to the bottom on pricing is a long-term revenue pressure worth watching.

sport.summary: NRL Round 17 wrap is in, with the Raiders winning in controversial fashion. Round 18 teams are being announced. Wimbledon kicked off today with Sinner and Swiatek defending their titles. And the AFL has a big story — a premiership-winning captain has been forced into immediate retirement.

stories.title: Controversial Bunker call helps Raiders win — Ricky Stuart's mid-game masterstroke dissected
stories.why_it_matters: The Raiders won a controversial Round 17 match after a disputed Bunker (video referee) call that Fox Sports says 'is not a try' — but the try was awarded anyway. Ricky Stuart also made a 'brutal' mid-game tactical switch that turned the match. With the Raiders on a bye in Round 18, they'll carry momentum into the back half of the season.

stories.title: AFL premiership-winning captain forced into immediate retirement
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL world is paying tribute after a premiership-winning captain was forced to announce his immediate retirement today. The AFL community has rallied around the player, with tributes flowing from clubs and teammates. Full details of the injury or health reason weren't available in the article text, but the retirement appears to have come suddenly and without warning.

stories.title: Fremantle Dockers set record for longest winning streak by a major WA sporting club
stories.why_it_matters: Fremantle Dockers beat the Gold Coast Suns to set a new record for the longest winning streak by any major WA sporting club — a historic milestone. The Dockers are flying in 2026 and the win over the local Suns will sting Gold Coast fans. Fremantle's run is drawing comparisons to some of the great winning streaks in Australian sport.

stories.title: Wimbledon 2026 opens: Sinner and Swiatek defend their titles on day one
stories.why_it_matters: Wimbledon 2026 got underway today with world number one Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek both in action defending their titles. It's a star-studded opening day at the All England Club. Australian Open experts are also tipping a US superstar to challenge a long-standing grand slam record during the fortnight — one to watch over the next two weeks.
